   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  NORWALK COMMUNITY PROMOTION COMMISSION
  December 8, 2025

Chair Leon called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. Responding to roll call were Vice Chair Ang,
Commissioner Sanchez, Commissioner Garcia and Commissioner Lopez. Also present was Levy Sun,
Director of Communications and Public Affairs, and Alex Ocegueda, Office Assistant III.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Sanchez made the motion and Commissioner Lopez seconded to approve the minutes
for November 10, 2025. There being no objection, the motion carried.

REPORTS

Holiday Home Decoration Contest

Ms. Ocegueda reported that, as of the meeting date, seven residential entries had been received and
no commercial entries had been submitted. Ms. Ocegueda distributed the door hangers created last
year and requested that Commissioners deliver them to decorated residences within the next few days
to encourage additional participation, as the submission deadline is at the end of the week. Ms.
Ocegueda also confirmed that judging packets would be delivered to Commissioners’ homes by the
end of the day on Thursday, December 18, allowing judging to take place from December 19 through
December 24.

Native Garden Contest

Ms. Ocegueda announced several opportunities for the Commission to promote the Native Plant
Garden Contest. The next outreach event will be Las Posadas, scheduled for Saturday, January 3,
from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at the Norwalk Sports Complex. Representatives from Cerritos College,
Ana Valcarcel and Joy Tsuhako, discussed potential participation through the distribution of
informational pamphlets, QR codes, native plant materials, and possible consultation offerings. Ms.
Tsuhako confirmed her availability to attend the Las Posadas event. Commissioners also discussed
future outreach opportunities, including Artastic and the Easter Egg Hunt, as well as booth engagement
strategies such as frequently asked questions (FAQ) materials, interactive activities, and visual
displays. Ms. Ocegueda noted that, due to the absence of business décor contest entries,
Commissioners may consider reallocating the business prize funds toward Cerritos College gift
certificates for starter plants and potential native garden consultations to be raffled at outreach events
to expand participation. Following discussion, Commissioners expressed interest in providing three (3)
$100 gift certificates for raffle. Ms. Ocegueda will review the budget and coordinate with Cerritos
College regarding the structure of the gift certificates, contingent upon the continued absence of
business contest entries. Mr. Sun reported that he had coordinated with vector control partners, who
indicated their support through the provision of a logo, a quote for the website, and educational
materials explaining the relationship between native plants and mosquito reduction.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Community Promotion Commission
December 8, 2025

Business Spotlight

Mr. Sun showed the “Keeping It Norwalk” Campaign, the November Small Businesses edition video to
Commissioners.

Merchandise Surveys

Commissioners discussed the launch of City-branded merchandise, beginning with simple, high-quality
cotton t-shirts. Considerations included pricing, minimum order quantities, size-based cost differentials,
and sleeve printing expenses, based on information provided by prospective vendors. Emphasis was
placed on partnering with local vendors whenever possible. Vendor-managed models were explored,
including options for online ordering, order fulfillment, customer pickup, and point-of-sale services, like
approaches utilized by other cities. Commissioners discussed the importance of avoiding City-managed
inventory and expressed interest in fixed per-item remittance models. Initial design concepts included
“Isle of Norwalk” and “Norwalk — Established 1957.” Color palette discussions favored neutral tones
and the avoidance of colors associated with gang affiliation. Commissioners will seek vendor quotes
and further evaluate fulfillment and sales models. The potential use of the Norwalk Town Square
signage on merchandise was briefly discussed and deferred pending further review and follow-up with
the relevant members of the Norwalk Town Square management team.

Communications and Public Affairs Analytics

Mr. Sun provided the analytics and explained Key Performance Indicators (KPI) and the city’s overall
reach across all outreach platforms for the last month. Mr. Sun reported that temporary access issues
with Meta analytics had been resolved and that the November social media engagement report would
proceed. Website analytics were reported as healthy, with a bounce rate slightly below 40 percent.

STAFF COMMENTS:

Ms. Ocegueda provided Commissioners with a list of the 2026 meeting and event dates at which their
attendance is expected. She also presented logo treatments for a new social media series titled Past
Forward, which focuses on Norwalk’s history and future context, for their consideration.
Commissioners unanimously selected the logo to be used for the series, and Ms. Ocegueda indicated
that the selected logo would be presented in full color at the next meeting. It was reported that
production is scheduled to begin in Winter 2025–26, with a target release of the first video in Spring
2026.

COMMISSIONERS COMMENTS:

Chair Leon expressed appreciation to Commissioners and staff for their support and coverage during
her absence at prior meetings. Commissioner Sanchez reported attending several community cultural
events and suggested engaging student musicians for future outreach activities. Vice Chair Ang
commented positively on the Christmas Tree Lighting event and shared observations from recent

community holiday outreach efforts. Commissioner Lopez reported receiving favorable community
feedback regarding the holiday events.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Public comment was received by Jack Cornejo regarding the merchandise items. A recommendation
was made to pursue a minimalist, high quality merchandise approach using existing city logos and
outsourced sales and fulfillment with a fixed per item return to the city. Jack encouraged the
Commission to avoid using trademarked or other sensitive colors and logos as they may be gang
affiliated and/or may promote a private company. No additional public comments were recorded.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:03 p.m.

_____________________________

Armida Leon, Chair
Community Promotion Commission
